DEFINITION.*** WHAT A SUBSYSTEM IS NOT ***: *** SUBSYSTEMS ARE AN ANALYTIC OVERLAY IMPOSED BY CYCLE 5. They are NOT declared anywhere in the repository. No package boundary, no __init__, no config, and no test corresponds to them, and NOTHING ENFORCES THEM. The MODULES and the IMPORT EDGES are FACTS (AST-derived). The GROUPING is a MODEL. ***

S06_media_analysis.cycle_7_assignment: framing_outcomes (added by #634) — the framing-outcome CONTRACT: WHY a clip was framed as it was, as first-class data. Level 0, imports NOTHING, consumed by framing + keyframes + reframe. It is NOT S01_foundation: that subsystem is defined as 'contracts and primitives with NO DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE', and this module is entirely domain.

S18_health_diag.cycle_7_assignment: reframe (added by #634) — `fanops reframe --dry-run`, a READ-ONLY corpus classification report. Assigned here because it MUTATES NOTHING; its closest analogue is `audit` (a read-only bucket table). *** THIS IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT AN OBVIOUS FACT: it exists to inform a MIGRATION, which is S19_maintenance's remit. Recorded as UNK-C7-1. If reframe ever grows a mutating verb, this assignment becomes wrong and it moves to S19. ***
S18_health_diag.cycle_7_assignment_RESOLVED: The condition above FIRED, and the answer held. #635 added `fanops reframe --apply` — but the mutation landed in a SEPARATE module (reframe_apply), dispatched from cli.py, and reframe.py itself was not touched. So the read-only report STAYS here and the mutating migration goes to S19_maintenance. UNK-C7-1 is resolved by construction rather than by re-assignment: the split the note anticipated is the split the code made.

S19_maintenance.origin_backfill_assignment: origin_backfill (added by MOL-756) — the one-shot reconstruction of `Moment.origin` for rows minted before the field existed, driven by the Studio Provenance panel with `fanops origin-backfill` as its headless twin. Assigned here for exactly the reason `stranded_posts` is: an out-of-band, snapshot-gated, reversible rewrite of stored state across the corpus, with no network anywhere in it. It is NOT S04_moments: S04 MINTS moments from an agent response; this touches one field on moments that already exist and can mint nothing. Its S18 import (audit) is LAZY, apply-path only, so no compile-time edge is added. The Studio half lives in S16 (actions_provenance / app_routes_provenance) — the same split S16/S19 already has for the wipe (studio.actions_wipe calls ledger_wipe).
S19_maintenance.stranded_posts_assignment: stranded_posts — `fanops posts reconcile-retired`, the one-time reconcile for posts left `awaiting_approval`/`queued` under a moment the re-decision cascade retired. Assigned here, not to S13_reconcile_metrics, because S13 reconciles LEDGER-vs-REMOTE state by polling a backend, and this touches no network at all: it is an out-of-band, snapshot-gated, reversible rewrite of stored state across the corpus — `paths_rebase` and `reframe_apply`'s shape exactly. Its S18 imports (audit, health_model) are LAZY, apply-path only, so no compile-time edge is added.
S19_maintenance.cycle_7_assignment: reframe_apply (added by #635) — `fanops reframe --apply`, the MUTATION phase of the reframe migration: a plan-driven, resumable, rollback-able re-render of clips that ALREADY EXIST. Assigned here, not to S09_render, because S09's members (clip, compose, produce, stitch_render) are the PRODUCTION PIPELINE that turns a moment into a new clip, and this is not in that pipeline — it is an out-of-band corpus migration that CALLS the renderer. Its closest analogue is `paths_rebase`: a one-off, careful, reversible rewrite of stored state across the whole corpus. That is S19's remit exactly. (The read-only dry-run REPORT stays in S18_health_diag; see the note there.)
